guard: the re-exec argv builder refuses an entry that is not the cotal composition root, and still accepts the three shapes a real install runs under
why: #1629: a fixture under tsx has `process.argv[1]` pointing at the suite, so the detached manager
`startManagerDetached` spawns IS the suite. On a persistent host that produced 970 generations
in 4.7 hours, each holding a nats-server and a delivery holder. The child is unref'd by design,
so no teardown owner can adopt it and the refusal has to be where the argv is built.
Both directions are mutated, because narrowness is the half that bites. `npm i -g cotal-ai`
publishes `<prefix>/bin/cotal` as a SYMLINK and Node leaves argv[1] on the link, which has no
extension: a guard that demanded one would refuse every global install's manager start while
still passing the headline cell. That was measured here before the regex was widened.

mutations.name: the guard is removed and any entry builds a re-exec argv again
mutations.expectRed: a `.smoke.ts` entry is REFUSED, not re-execed as a daemon

mutations.name: the entry must carry an extension, so a global install's bin symlink is refused
mutations.expectRed: a bare `cotal` bin symlink (the global-install shape) builds a re-exec argv
